context: Fiore defends disappointing treasure; Cyrus excavates an ancient warrior's grave; party seeks liquor shop. E4390-E4399 and E4480-E4489 reviewed.
decisions: Damaged epitaph remains incomplete. Ryud, Morellen Street and Pezik Liquor Store follow shared provisional glossary spellings. Imported rows preserved. Cross-row clauses retain boundaries.
provenance: Two exact-match imported rows preserved; 78 new English translations from Japanese source with adjacent context reviewed.

translations.en: Isn't there anything else?
Ugh. What a letdown...
No, no, no. Maybe this equipment
could be valuable too.
We just need to take it back and have it appraised.
We don't know for sure it's junk yet!
You found a sign that read Leiden Street.
A fierce battle or perhaps a fire must once have taken place here.
The sign was partly scorched,
and something dried and discolored, probably blood,
clung to it in places.
Signs of a battle? Everything around here's wrecked too.
Maybe their pursuers burned the place.
Anyway, let's look for the broken statue.
You found what appeared to be a broken stone statue.
Rather than falling over and shattering, it looked as though
it had been smashed with a metal club.
This might not be the broken statue mentioned in the journal,
but searching nearby might reveal the warrior's grave.
This has to be the statue from the journal.
There can't just happen to be lots of broken statues
near the Leiden Street sign.
If there were, they wouldn't make much of a landmark.
Come on, let's find the burial site!
It was far too simple for a warrior's grave:
just a wooden stake driven into the ground as a marker.
An epitaph had apparently been carved there.
Rough marks gouged with a dagger remained on part of it.
The epitaph had faded,
"Beloved... Ryu... lies... here..."
translations.note: Damaged epitaph retains only the source's name fragment.

translations.en: and little more than that was legible.
This must be where the warrior's buried.
Hurry, let's dig it up!
You calmed the impatient @7rCyrus@0r and offered a prayer,
then began digging up the grave.
If the burial took place during their flight, there would be no coffin.
You dug carefully to avoid damaging any remains you found,
until a thick, sturdy cloth stained with mud came into view.
Could this be the warrior @7rRyud@0r?
As though triggered by @7rCyrus's@0r words,
something wrapped in the cloth shook off the mud
and slowly rose.
No... Has the warrior become undead?!
Tainted by the monsters' miasma during the attack, the warrior's corpse
had become an Undead Knight over the centuries.
No... A warrior who fought alongside @7rChu Lu Gah@0r,
reduced to an undead creature...
Wait. What about the warrior's equipment?
@7rCyrus@0r hurried over to the fallen warrior's remains
and began checking the equipment, but his shoulders soon slumped.
He looked at you apologetically.
It's no good. The metal's corroded.
At this point, I think a weapon from any shop
would have a better edge.
Wait! What else was buried here...?
@7rCyrus@0r examined the excavated grave for a little while,
then quickly looked up and shook his head.
Nothing. All we gained was the knowledge
that @7rChu Lu Gah's@0r warrior companion had become undead.
That's all...
It can't be helped. We shouldn't linger here.
Let's bury the remains properly and go back to town.
Urged on by a thoroughly disappointed @7rCyrus@0r,
you left the grave behind.
An old sign with the name Morellen Street carved into it
was nailed to the passage wall.
Oooh! Here it is!
The liquor shop should be somewhere around here!
You casually picked up an old board lying on the ground
and found the name Pezik Liquor Store written on it.
Looks like it must be around here, doesn't it?
I've heard some monsters like a drink too, so let's be careful!
You found a box with a tankard drawn on its lid.
The moment you touched it, the box suddenly began speaking.
Tankard Box
Welcome, welcome.
If you wish to take the liquor inside me,
please answer my question. Is that clear?
The monster slowly topples over,
